steps.reply:
Simplifications, behaviour-preserving:

- `result = result + char` → `result += char`. Same effect, less noise.
- Build list, `"".join(...)` at end. Avoids O(n²) string concat on long input. Behaviour same, faster.
- `previous.isalpha()` branch → track boolean `prev_alpha` instead of full char. Skip re-checking `isalpha` semantics but same result since only that property used. Marginal.
- Loop reads clearer as:
  ```python
  prev_alpha = False
  out = []
  for ch in text:
      out.append(ch.lower() if prev_alpha else ch.upper())
      prev_alpha = ch.isalpha()
  return "".join(out)
  ```
- Docstring at top-of-module duplicates function docstring. Drop module docstring or shorten one.
- Sentinel `previous = " "` works only because space is non-alpha. Boolean `prev_alpha=False` makes intent explicit, kills magic value.

No stdlib one-liner matches exactly (`str.title()` differs on apostrophes/digits — would change behaviour). Keep hand-rolled loop.

input.text: Look at textkit/slugify.py and suggest how to keep accented letters (é becomes e) instead of dropping them. Don't change anything yet.

steps.reply:
Approach, stdlib only:

- Import `unicodedata`.
- Before loop: normalize+strip combining marks.
  ```python
  normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
  folded = "".join(c for c in normalized if not unicodedata.combining(c))
  ```
  NFKD splits `é` → `e` + combining acute; filter drops the accent. Also fixes ligatures (`ﬁ`→`fi`).
- Then `.lower()` (or better `.casefold()`) as before, loop unchanged.
- Swap `text.lower()` for `text.casefold()` so `ß`→`ss`, `İ`→`i̇`→`i` after the strip.

Placement: two lines at start of `slugify`, replace `text.lower()` in the `for` with the folded string.

Limits worth flagging:
- `æ ø ð þ` don't decompose in NFKD — still dropped. Need explicit map if wanted.
- Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Greek) not transliterated — still dropped. Full transliteration needs `unidecode` (third-party).
- If tests assert current drop-behaviour for accented input, they'll break — check tests first.

No behaviour change until asked.
